query: Fair Copies Wanted {A notice in a shaky hand. A student down with fever needs a fortnight of lecture notes copied out fair, and will pay for neatness.|Another fever, another fortnight of notes to copy fair. The notice says "neat hand preferred", and someone has written your name beside it.|The copying notice again. By now you can copy a page without reading a word of it, if you want to.} Copy them for the pay {Two evenings of careful letters. The pay arrives with a note that says your sevens are beautiful.|You copy every page, blot nothing and are paid exactly. Your wrist aches until the weekend.|You copy without reading, as fast as the ink allows. The pay is fair and the evening is gone.} Copy them slowly, and learn them too {You read as you copy. Half the pay goes on candles, and you learn a course you aren't even taking.|You copy slowly and read every line. The notes are better than your own, and you keep a few of the ideas.|You read it all, slowly. The student pays a little less for the delay, and you know a little more for it.}
